details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:3737-3774 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_pr_priority_lane_pressure` works out the starvation-cap origin again on every tick from the oldest priority run queued at that moment (`| sort_by(.c) | first`, `.c + $wait_s`), and nothing saves when each PR was first skipped or when the hold began. So when the oldest priority run leaves the queue while a younger one is still queued, the origin moves forward and the cap clock restarts for every held PR.
  WHY: Priority runs that overlap in the queue can keep a non-priority PR at `outcome=deferred reason=priority_run_queued` past PRIORITY_LANE_MAX_DEFER_MINUTES, possibly indefinitely, which breaks issue #10048's rule that no PR is held longer than a cap "measured from the first skip". The callers are scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:302-310 and :324 (`since=` is rewritten each tick) and scripts/review_merge_train.sh:1870/1883 (`_MT_PRIORITY_LANE_HOLD_SINCE`). Three reviewers rated this MAJOR and gemini gave no severity.
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:377-387 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The early `_pr_priority_lane_decide final_ci ...` call (fci_lane_done=true) runs before `[ "${checked}" -lt "${max}" ] || continue`. A non-priority head with gate success that is past the cap is therefore logged as `outcome=released reason=max_defer surface=final_ci` and then skipped without notice once FINAL_CI_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK is used up.
  WHY: The logs report releases for heads that got no final-CI dispatch that tick and no counter records the skip, which misleads operators and log analysis. The head is still retried on a later tick. Three reviewers rated this NIT and gemini gave no severity.
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:_pr_priority_lane_decide (MERGE_TRAIN_PRIORITY_LABELS) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Setting PRIORITY_LANE_ENABLED=false does not bring back today's behaviour, because the global MERGE_TRAIN_PRIORITY_LABELS default now includes ai:priority.
  WHY: PRs linked to an ai:priority issue still bypass non-priority merge-train blockers with the switch off. Gemini gave no severity. openai_gpt-6-luna rated the same root cause MAJOR as a task gap (see CONSENSUS TASK GAPS). z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly declined to report it, saying issue #10048 step 1 requires the unconditional default.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Create the `ai:priority` label where the pipeline creates its other labels." (issue #10048, Approach step 5 / Implementation step 5)
  expected_change_site: scripts/label_helpers.sh `_AI_LABEL_COLORS` (lines 23-91) and `_AI_LABEL_DESCS` (lines 93-160), plus the matching `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json` entry
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/label_helpers.sh has no "ai:priority" entry in either catalogue, and .github/ai/label_contract.v1.json has none either. Neither the PR diff nor the LAST RUN DIFF touches these files. The label is only created lazily, through `ensure_label_exists "ai:priority"` in review_sweep_annotate_head_gate (scripts/review_sweep_head_gate.sh:168), and only when the lane is on and the GraphQL lookup returns null. That path falls back to colour `1d76db` and the description "AI workflow label" (scripts/label_helpers.sh:185-186), and the normal label precreation paths never create the label. Severity disagreement: sonnet and gemini rated it MAJOR, luna and glm rated it NIT.
- requirement: "With the switch off, or with no labelled issue, every dispatch decision is identical to today's."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`, priority-label parsing and merge-train priority checks
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The `MERGE_TRAIN_PRIORITY_LABELS` default includes `ai:priority` at lines 233-243. The blocker-bypass checks at lines 449-489 use that list without checking `PRIORITY_LANE_ENABLED`. README.md:251 documents this as an exception instead of restoring the old behaviour. Rated MAJOR. z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly did not report this, citing issue #10048 step 1 and the documented rollback (set the variable to `ai:workflow-heal,ai:security`).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/pr_checks_lib.sh:_pr_priority_lane_pressure, jq tail "| sort_by(.c) | first | if . == null then empty else \"\(.p) \((($now - .c) / 60) | floor) \(.c + $wait_s)\" end" (used as <hold_since_epoch> by _pr_priority_lane_decide, review_sweep_priority_lane_hold, _mt_priority_lane_defer_for_base) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The starvation-cap origin is worked out again each tick from the oldest priority run queued at that moment, and no hold-start marker survives between ticks. When that run leaves the queue, the origin jumps forward to the next run's created_at plus the wait, and every held PR's cap clock restarts.
  WHY: With overlapping priority runs (review, security-audit and final-CI), non-priority PRs stay `outcome=deferred reason=priority_run_queued` past PRIORITY_LANE_MAX_DEFER_MINUTES. This breaks the issue's "No PR is held back for longer than a cap", measured from the first skip. Suggested fix: carry the earliest since= across ticks while hold=true, or take the minimum of the stored and new origins.
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:lines 377-387 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The early `_pr_priority_lane_decide final_ci ...` call (fci_lane_done=true) runs before `[ "${checked}" -lt "${max}" ] || continue`, so a head past the cap is logged as released and then skipped once FINAL_CI_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK is used up, with no counter recording the skip.
  WHY: The logs report a release for a PR that got no dispatch that tick, which misleads operators and log analysis. The head is retried later. Hardening suggestion (lines 378-380): add `&& [ "${checked}" -lt "${max}" ]` to the early-decide condition, or move the cap check before the decide (1-2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Create the `ai:priority` label where the pipeline creates its other labels." (issue #10048, Approach step 5 and Implementation step 5. scripts/label_helpers.sh is in the plan grant's files_touched.)
  Expected change site: scripts/label_helpers.sh, the _AI_LABEL_COLORS map (next to "ai:security" at line 76 and "ai:workflow-heal" at line 81) and the description map (next to lines 146 and 151), plus whatever label contract test or file pairs with that catalogue.
  Evidence of absence: There is no "ai:priority" entry, and neither the PR diff nor the LAST RUN DIFF touches the file. The only creation path is the lazy `ensure_label_exists "ai:priority"` in review_sweep_annotate_head_gate, which uses the fallback colour and no catalogue description. Normal precreation never creates the label, and the linked issue does not defer it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The early final-CI deferral call runs before the per-tick cap check ([ "${checked}" -lt "${max}" ] || continue).
  WHY: PRs past the cap are logged with outcome=released reason=max_defer and then skipped silently when the per-tick cap is reached, which makes the logs confusing and the sweep metrics wrong.

  WHY: The log reports the PR as released for dispatch, but the cap skips it silently and no final-CI dispatch happens that tick.
